gummer: A punch-cutting tool, or machine for deepening and enlarging the spaces between the teeth of a worn saw.
gulgul: A cement made in India from sea shells, pulverized and mixed with oil, and spread over a ship's bottom, to prevent the boring of worms.
gusset: 1. A small piece of cloth inserted in a garment, for the purpose of strengthening some part or giving it a tapering enlargement. Seam and gusset and band. Hood. 2. Anything resembling a gusset in a garment; as: (a) (Armor) A small piece of chain mail at the openings of the joints beneath the arms.
gurglet: A porous earthen jar for cooling water by evaporation.
gustoso: Tasteful; in a tasteful, agreeable manner.
guaiac: Pertaining to, or resembling, guaiacum. -- n. Guaiacum.
gutturo: A combining form denoting relation to the throat; as, gutturo- nasal, having both a guttural and a nasal character; gutturo-palatal.
guipure: A term used for lace of different kinds; most properly for a lace of large pattern and heavy material which has no ground or mesh, but has the pattern held together by connecting threads called bars or brides.
gumboil: A small suppurting inflamed spot on the gum.
guarana: A preparation from the seeds of Paullinia sorbilis, a woody climber of Brazil, used in making an astringent drink, and also in the cure of headache.
guttatrap: The inspissated juice of a tree of the genus Artocarpus (A. incisa, or breadfruit tree), sometimes used in making birdlime, on account of its glutinous quality.
guerdonable: Worthy of reward. Sir G. Buck.
gula: 1. (Zoöl.) (a) The upper front of the neck, next to the chin; the upper throat. (b) A plate which in most insects supports the submentum. 2. (Arch.) A capping molding. Same as Cymatium.
gue: A sharper; a rogue. (old) J. Webstar.
gutwort: A plant, Globularia Alypum, a violent purgative, found in Africa.
guest: 1. A visitor; a person received and entertained in one's house or at one's table; a visitor entertained without pay. To cheer his gueste, whom he had stayed that night. Spenser. | To receive or entertain hospitably. (old) Sylvester.
gunnel: 1. A gunwale. 2. (Zoöl.) A small, eel-shaped, marine fish of the genus Murænoides; esp., M. gunnellus of Europe and America; -- called also gunnel fish, butterfish, rock eel.
gunpowder: A black, granular, explosive substance, consisting of an intimate mechanical mixture of niter, charcoal, and sulphur. It is used in gunnery and blasting. Note: Gunpowder consists of from 70 to 80 per cent of niter, with 10 to 15 per cent of each of the other ingredients.
guarantor: (a) One who makes or gives a guaranty; a warrantor; a surety. (b) One who engages to secure another in any right or possession.
guerite: A projecting turret for a sentry, as at the salient angles of works, or the acute angles of bastions.
guereza: A beautiful Abyssinian monkey (Colobus guereza), having the body black, with a fringe of long, silky, white hair along the sides, and a tuft of the same at the end of the tail. The frontal band, cheeks, and chin are white.
guinea: 1. A district on the west coast of Africa (formerly noted for its export of gold and slaves) after which the Guinea fowl, Guinea grass, Guinea peach, etc., are named. 2. gunstick: A stick to ram down the charge of a musket, etc.; a rammer or ramrod.
guesswarp: A rope or hawser by which a vessel is towed or warped along; -- so called because it is necessary to guess at the length to be carried in the boat making the attachment to a distant object.
gurt: A gutter or channel for water, hewn out of the bottom of a working drift. Page.
guara: (a) The scarlet ibis. See Ibis. (b) A large-maned wild dog of South America (Canis jubatus) -- named from its cry.
guilloche: An ornament in the form of two or more bands or strings twisted over each other in a continued series, leaving circular openings which are filled with round ornaments.
guardable: Capable of being guarded or protected.
guelf: One of a faction in Germany and Italy, in the 12th and 13th centuries, which supported the House of Guelph and the pope, and opposed the Ghibellines, or faction of the German emperors.
guidguid: A South American ant bird of the genus Hylactes; -- called also barking bird.
guaranine: An alkaloid extracted from guarana. Same as Caffeine.

guze: A roundlet of tincture sanguine, which is blazoned without mention of the tincture.
guidable: Capable of being guided; willing to be guided or counseled. Sprat.
gusty: Subject to, or characterized by, gusts or squalls; windy; stormy; tempestuous. Upon a raw and gusty day. Shak.
gust: 1. A sudden squall; a violent blast of wind; a sudden and brief rushing or driving of the wind. Snow, and hail, stormy gust and flaw. Milton. 2. A sudden violent burst of passion. Bacon. | 1. gut: 1. A narrow passage of water; as, the Gut of Canso. 2. An intenstine; a bowel; the whole alimentary canal; the enteron; (pl.) bowels; entrails. 3. gushing: 1. Rushing forth with violence, as a fluid; flowing copiously; as, gushing waters. "Gushing blood." Milton. 2. Emitting copiously, as tears or words; weakly and unreservedly demonstrative in matters of affection; sentimental. [Colloq.]
guardsman: 1. One who guards; a guard. 2. A member, either officer or private, of any military body called Guards.
gumminess: The state or quality of being gummy; viscousness.
guardian: 1. One who guards, preserves, or secures; one to whom any person or thing is committed for protection, security, or preservation from injury; a warden. 2. guarded: Cautious; wary; circumspect; as, he was guarded in his expressions; framed or uttered with caution; as, his expressions were guarded. -- Guard"edly, adv. -- Guard"ed*ness, n.
gudgeon: 1. (Zoöl.) A small European freshwater fish (Gobio fluviatilis), allied to the carp. It is easily caught and often used for food and for bait. gun: 1. A weapon which throws or propels a missile to a distance; any firearm or instrument for throwing projectiles by the explosion of gunpowder, consisting of a tube or barrel closed at one end, in… | To practice fowling or hunting small game; -- chiefly in participial form; as, to go gunning.
guiltsick: Made sick by consciousness of guilt. "A guilt-sick conscience." Beau. c& El.

gulleting: A system of excavating by means of gullets or channels.

gutturine: Pertaining to the throat. (old) "Gutturine tumor." Ray.
guardant: 1. Acting as guardian. (old) Shak. 2. (Her.) Same as Gardant.
gumbo: 1. A soup thickened with the mucilaginous pods of the okra; okra soup. 2. The okra plant or its pods.
guige: The leather strap by which the shield of a knight was slung across the shoulder, or across the neck and shoulder. Meyrick (Ancient Armor).

guelderrose: A cultivated variety of a species of Viburnum (V. Opulus), bearing large bunches of white flowers; -- called also snowball tree.
gullible: Easily gulled; that may be duped. -- Gul"li*bii`i*ty, n. Burke.
guitguit: One of several species of small tropical American birds of the family Coerebidæ, allied to the creepers; -- called also quit. See Quit.

gurge: A whirlpool. (old) The plain, wherein a black bituminous gurge Boils out from under ground. Milton.
guise: 1. guttifer: A plant that exudes gum or resin.

guilty: 1. gurl: A young person of either sex. (old) See Girl. Chaucer.
gulfy: Full of whirlpools or gulfs. Chapman.
guesser: One who guesses; one who forms or gives an opinion without means of knowing.
guestrope: The line by which a boat makes fast to the swinging boom. Ham. Nav. Encyc.
gunny: A strong, coarse kind of sacking, made from the fibers (called jute) of two plants of the genus Corchorus (C. olitorius and C. capsularis), of India. The fiber is also used in the manufacture of cordage. Gunny bag, a sack made of gunny, used for coarse commodities.
guardianship: The office, duty, or care, of a guardian; protection; care; watch.
guilder: A Dutch silver coin worth about forty cents; -- called also florin and gulden.
gumma: A kind of soft tumor, usually of syphilitic origin.

guineapigdirector: A director (usually one holding a number of directorships) who serves merely or mainly for the fee (in England, often a guinea) paid for attendance. [Colloq.]

guib: A West African antelope (Tragelaphus scriptus), curiously marked with white stripes and spots on a reddish fawn ground, and hence called harnessed antelope; -- called also guiba.
gustful: Tasteful; well-tasted. (old) Sir K. Digby. -- Gust"ful*ness, n. (old) Barrow. | Gusty. A gustful April morn. Tennyson.
guacharo: A nocturnal bird of South America and Trinidad (Steatornis Caripensis, or S. steatornis); -- called also oilbird. Note: It resembles the goatsuckers and nighthawks, but feeds on fruits, and nests in caverns. A pure oil, used in place of butter, is extracted from the young by the natives.
guillemot: One of several northern sea birds, allied to the auks. They have short legs, placed far back, and are expert divers and swimmers. guttulous: In droplike form. (old) In its [hail's] guttulous descent from the air. Sir T. Browne.
gutturalism: The quality of being guttural; as, the gutturalism of A [in the 16th cent.] Earle.
guesswork: Work performed, or results obtained, by guess; conjecture.
gushingly: , adv. 1. In a gushing manner; copiously. Byron. 2. Weakly; sentimentally; effusively. [Colloq.]
gummosity: Gumminess; a viscous or adhesive quality or nature. Floyer.
guilor: A deceiver; one who deludes, or uses guile. (old) Spenser.

guffaw: A loud burst of laughter, a horse laugh. "A hearty low guffaw." Carlyle.
guanaco: A South American mammal (Auchenia huanaco), allied to the llama, but of larger size and more graceful form, inhabiting the southern Andes and Patagonia. It is supposed by some to be the llama in a wild state. [Written also huanaco.]
guttated: Besprinkled with drops, or droplike spots. Bailey.
gutturize: To make in the throat; to gutturalize. For which the Germans gutturize a sound. Coleridge.

guacho: 1. One of the mixed-blood (Spanish-Indian) inhabitants of the pampas of South America; a mestizo. 2. An Indian who serves as a messenger.

gurlet: A pickax with one sharp point and one cutting edge. Knight.
gurjun: A thin balsam or wood oil derived from the Diptcrocarpus lævis, an East Indian tree. It is used in medicine, and as a substitute for linseed oil in the coarser kinds of paint.
gustation: The act of tasting. Sir T. Browne.
guidage: 1. The reward given to a guide for services. Ainsworth. 2. Guidance; lead; direction. Southey.
guava: A tropical tree, or its fruit, of the genus Psidium. Two varieties are well known, the P. pyriferum, or white guava, and P. pomiferum, or red guava. The fruit or berry is shaped like a pomegranate, but is much smaller. It is somewhat astringent, but makes a delicious jelly.

guardroom: The room occupied by the guard during its term of duty; also, a room where prisoners are confined.

guttiferous: (a) Yielding gum or resinous substances. (b) Pertaining to a natural order of trees and shrubs (Guttiferæ) noted for their abounding in a resinous sap.
guelfic: Of or pertaining to the family or the facttion of the Guelphs.

guimpe: A kind of short chemisette, worn with a low-necked dress.

guttate: Spotted, as if discolored by drops.

guelph: One of a faction in Germany and Italy, in the 12th and 13th centuries, which supported the House of Guelph and the pope, and opposed the Ghibellines, or faction of the German emperors.

guitar: A stringed instrument of music resembling the lute or the violin, but larger, and having six strings, three of silk covered with silver wire, and three of catgut, -- played upon with the fingers.
gulp: To swallow eagerly, or in large draughts; to swallow up; to take down at one swallow. He does not swallow, but he gulps it down. Cowper. The old man . . . glibly gulped down the whole narrative. | 1. The act of taking a large mouthful; a swallow, or as much as is awallowed at once. 2. A disgorging. [Colloq.]
guidance: The act or result of guiding; the superintendence or assistance of a guide; direction; government; a leading. His studies were without guidance and without plan. Macaulay.
gunstome: A cannon ball; -- so called because originally made of stone. (old) Shak.
guiser: A person in disguise; a masker; a mummer. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.]
guano: A substance found in great abundance on some coasts or islands frequented by sea fowls, and composed chiefly of their excrement. It is rich in phosphates and ammonia, and is used as a powerful fertilizer.
gunlock: The lock of a gun, for producing the discharge. See Lock.
gubernatorial: Pertaining to a governor, or to government.
gurnet: One ofseveral European marine fishes, of the genus Trigla and allied genera, having a large and spiny head, with mailed cheeks. Some of the species are highly esteemed for food. The name is sometimes applied to the American sea robins. [Written also gournet.] Plyling gurnard. See under Flying.
guidepost: A post at the fork of a road, with a guideboard on it, to direct travelers.
gullery: An act, or the practice, of gulling; trickery; fraud. "A mere gullery." Selden.
guttle: To put into the gut; to swallow greedily; to gorge; to gormandize. (old) L'Estrange. Dryden.
guenon: One of several long-tailed Oriental monkeys, of the genus Cercocebus, as the green monkey and grivet.
guideboard: A board, as upon a guidepost having upon it directions or information as to the road. Lowell.
gunflint: A sharpened flint for the lock of a gun, to ignite the charge. It was in common use before the introduction of percussion caps.
gunnie: Space left by the removal of ore.
guilt: 1. The criminality and consequent exposure to punishment resulting from willful disobedience of law, or from morally wrong action; teh state of one who has broken a moral or political law; crime; criminality; offense against right. Satan had not answer, but stood struck With guilt of his own sin. Milton. 2. Exposure to any legal penalty or forfeiture.
gunsmith: One whose occupation is to make or repair small firearms; an armorer. | The art or business of a gunsmith.
gunreach: The reach or distance to which a gun will shoot; gunshot.
gutter: 1. A channel at the eaves of a roof for conveying away the rain; an eaves channel; an eaves trough. 2. A small channel at the roadside or elsewhere, to lead off surface water. | 1. To cut or form into small longitudinal hollows; to channel. Shak. 2. To supply with a gutter or gutters. Dryden.
guestwise: In the manner of a guest.
guaiacol: A colorless liquid, C7H8O2, with a peculiar odor. It is the methyl ether of pyrocatechin, and is obtained by distilling guaiacum from wood-tar creosote, and in other ways. It has been used in treating pulmonary tuberculosis.
guardful: Cautions; wary; watchful. [Obs. or Poetic.] -- Guard"ful*ly, adv.
gutturality: The quality of being guttural. "The old gutturality of k." Earle.
guards: A body of picked troops; as, "The Household Guards."
guile: Craft; deceitful cunning; artifice; duplicity; wile; deceit; treachery. Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile. John i. 47. To wage by force or guile eternal war. Milton. | To disguise or conceal; to deceive or delude. (old) Spenser.
gummite: A yellow amorphous mineral, essentially a hydrated oxide of uranium derived from the alteration of uraninite.
gurry: An alvine evacuation; also, refuse matter. [Obs. or Local] Holland.
guttapercha: A concrete juice produced by various trees found in the Malayan archipelago, especially by the Isonandra, or Dichopsis, Gutta. It becomes soft, and unpressible at the tamperature of boiling water, and, on cooling, retains its new shape. It dissolves in oils and ethers, but not in water.
guiltless: 1. Free from guilt; innocent. The Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain. Ex. xx. 7. 2. Without experience or trial; unacquainted (with). Such gardening tools, as art, yet rude, Guiltless of fire, had formed. Milton. -- Guilt"less*ly, adv. -- Guilt"less*ness, n.
gunning: The act or practice of hunting or shooting game with a gun. The art of gunning was but little practiced. Goldsmith.
gummous: 1. Gumlike, or composed of gum; gummy. 2. (Med.) Of or pertaining to a gumma.
